Phosphocreatine serves as a rapidly available reserve of high-energy phosphates in skeletal muscle, primarily for the regeneration of ATP from ADP during intense activity.  
It is synthesized and stored in the cytoplasm, where it can quickly supply energy to the myofibrils.  
It is not stored in mitochondria, the sarcolemma, or all subcellular compartments.
